groups.title: Oral liquid (158631ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle (100 mg as iron) once a day. Children aged 12 years to under 19 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 2 times a day. Children aged 1 year to under 12 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 1 to 2 times a day. Take the dose before a meal, during a meal or after a meal.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which abnormal iron metabolism causes iron to be deposited in the liver and pancreas), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, impaired iron utilisation, iron overload, anaemia due to bone marrow failure, chronic haemolytic anaemia, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis or liver cirrhosis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis, impaired cardiac or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney impairment or low blood protein.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with iron-containing preparations (iron supplements, liver contrast agents for MRI and the like), anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene, diphosphonates, thyroxine, cefdinir preparations, quinolones, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, vitamin E preparations, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If hives, itching, skin hypersensitivity on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, coma, occasional rises in AST and ALT, rare rises in ALP, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, discoloration of the teeth or stomach discomfort appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Lotion (340500CLT)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve pain and inflammation from sprains, bruises, muscle pain, joint pain, fracture pain, low back pain, stiff shoulders, neuralgia, rheumatic pain, itchy skin, insect bites and chilblains (frostbite injuries).
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 to 4 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine on infants aged 30 months or under, in or around the eyes, on mucous membranes and the like, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like, on wounded skin, or on sensitive skin.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had an allergic reaction to a medicine or a cosmetic, if you have an allergic constitution, if you have severe wet or eroded (macerated) skin, if you have a circulatory disorder or diabetes, if the user is a child aged 12 years or under, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Use this medicine externally only; it must not be used internally. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, rinse the eyes with water immediately. Do not wrap or bandage the treated area, and do not expose it to external heat or hot water.

If symptoms such as rash, redness or itching appear as a result of using this medicine, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (490700ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin B6 during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after illness, to relieve the symptoms of angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation of the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis, and for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 10 mL at a time, 3 times a day, between meals (between one meal and the next).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have severe kidney failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein, if you are pregnant, or if you are hypersensitive to caramel.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If red spots, diarrhoea, cardiac arrest or signs of reduced central nervous system function appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (267200ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: Adults: take 20 mL at a time. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 13 mL at a time. Ages 8 years to under 11 years: 10 mL at a time. Ages 5 years to under 8 years: 7 mL at a time. Ages 3 years to under 5 years: 5 mL at a time. Ages 2 years to under 3 years: 4 mL at a time. Take the dose 3 to 4 times a day, after meals and at bedtime.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a constitution that makes allergy likely; if you have hypersensitivity to caramel or have had a reaction to it; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, a high fever, heart disease or high blood pressure, or if you are debilitated; if the user is an older person; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom the medicine is essential.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), other antitussives and expectorants, cold medicines, antihistamines, sedatives or alcohol. Do not take this medicine if you stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), anxiety, tremor or insomnia appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (D66700ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 1 sachet (20 mL) at a time. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 2/3 sachet at a time. Ages 7 years to under 11 years: 1/2 sachet at a time. Ages 3 years to under 7 years: 1/3 sachet at a time. Ages 2 years to under 3 years: 1/4 sachet at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have ever had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have a constitution that makes hives, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy likely; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough (associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take this medicine continuously over a long period. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). If you are being given medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (rarely, hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A18900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 12 years and over: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time, every 4 hours. Do not take more than 8 tablets in 1 day, counting the daytime product and the night-time product together.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza (if there is a change in behaviour accompanied by nausea or vomiting, consult a doctor, because it may be an early sign of Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious illness); if you or a family member has a constitution that makes hives, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy likely; if you have had an allergic reaction; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated, has a high fever or is a child under 12 years of age; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you are under a doctor's care (medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids and the like); or if you have a cough (associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take this medicine continuously over a long period. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive (cough suppressant), an expectorant (phlegm medicine), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines), with medicines for high or low blood pressure, or with phenylephrine hydrochloride, pseudoephedrine hydrochloride or salicylates. Take care when taking it with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, because they may increase the plasma half-life of acetaminophen.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, headache, wheezing, asthma, yellow or green phlegm, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives, chest tightness, a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, difficulty breathing and the like), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), impaired liver function, interstitial pneumonia, low platelet count, low white blood cell count, pancytopenia, neutropenia or agranulocytosis appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If there is no improvement after several (5 to 6) doses, if pain lasts for 5 days or more after taking the medicine, if fever lasts for 3 days or more, or if a blocked nose lasts for 7 days or more or gets worse, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic respiratory disorders with increased secretion, such as acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchitis accompanied by breathing difficulty (asthma, cough), nasopharyngitis and laryngotracheitis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 capsules (200 mg) at a time, 2 times a day.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding.

If a generalised allergic reaction (reddening of the skin, itching, a burning feeling) or a local reaction — which occur rarely — appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye drops (216134COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for dry eyes and when wearing hard contact lenses.
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops into the eye at a time, 4 to 5 times a day. The amount is increased or decreased as appropriate according to symptoms.
groups.caution:
Avoid wearing soft contact lenses during treatment. Use this medicine only in the eye. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing the product with others where possible.

Very rarely, a hypersensitivity reaction may occur.

groups.title: Syrup (C89800ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 sachet at a time, 3 times a day, leaving at least 4 hours between doses and taking only the smallest stated amount. Dissolve 1 sachet in about 250 mL of hot water that is not boiling, and drink it within 10 to 15 minutes.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor or have taken one within the past 2 weeks; if you have breathing difficulty caused by an asthma attack, emphysema or chronic bronchitis; if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, a lower urinary tract obstructive disease, stenosing peptic ulcer, pyloroduodenal obstruction, high blood pressure, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severely reduced heart function, epilepsy or phaeochromocytoma; if you have aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics) or have had it in the past; if you have diabetes; if you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol; if the user is a child under 18 years of age; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you are breast-feeding; if you have a hereditary problem such as glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, sucrase deficiency, or fructose or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you have phenylketonuria and need to restrict phenylalanine intake, because this medicine contains aspartame which is metabolised to phenylalanine; or if the user is an older person with confusion.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a constitution that makes allergy likely, Raynaud's syndrome, myasthenia gravis, liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have had a peptic ulcer; if you have a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed (abnormal platelet function); if you have abnormal heart function, thyroid disease or porphyria; if you have had pre-eclampsia; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is an older person; if you have a cough with a lot of phlegm; if you have obstructive vascular disease, closed-angle glaucoma, bronchitis or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); or if you have hypersensitivity to Red No. 40.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness, dizziness, reduced vision and impaired cognitive and psychomotor function may occur, so avoid driving and operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), other products containing diphenhydramine, antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, sleeping medicines, antihistamines, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, other sympathomimetic medicines (decongestants, appetite suppressants, amphetamines and the like), antihypertensive medicines (vasodilators, beta-blockers, debrisoquine, guanethidine, reserpine, methyldopa and the like), metoclopramide, domperidone, cholestyramine, warfarin, coumarin anticoagulants, anticholinergic medicines, chloramphenicol, zidovudine, probenecid, digoxin and cardiac glycosides, or ergot alkaloids (ergotamine, methysergide).

If acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis appears; if a severe sore throat, or a sore throat with fever, headache, rash, nausea or vomiting, lasts for 2 days or more; if fever lasts for 3 days or more, or cough or a blocked nose lasts for 7 days or more; or if signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, hives and the like), asthma, low platelet count, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia (destruction of red blood cells), methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure), dizziness, drowsiness, nervousness, insomnia, sedation, lassitude, a heavy head, convulsions, abnormal sensation, dyskinesia, muscle cramps, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, thirst, excessive lowering of body temperature, collapse, cold limbs, a rise in blood pressure or reflex slow heartbeat appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (A50700ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a head cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 24 mL at a time. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 16 mL at a time. Ages 7 years to under 11 years: 12 mL at a time. Ages 3 years to under 7 years: 8 mL at a time. Ages 2 years to under 3 years: 6 mL at a time. Take the dose 4 times a day, after each meal and, if needed, before going to bed. If necessary, it may be taken up to 6 times in 1 day, about every 4 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, swelling, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision), difficulty passing urine, thyroid disease or diabetes; if you are debilitated or have a high fever; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is an older person; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other oral medicines for rhinitis, or with oral medicines that contain an antihistamine (cold medicines, antitussives and expectorants, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines and the like). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide). Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If haemorrhagic stroke, nausea, vomiting, thirst (persistent or severe), constipation, loss of appetite, rash, redness, itching or difficulty passing urine appears, or — rarely — shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), or if the amount of urine decreases, the face and limbs swell, the eyelids feel heavy, the hands become stiff, blood pressure rises, or headache, weakness, cramp of the arms or legs or paralysis appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, within 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is an older person or is debilitated; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a high fever; if you have stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or ulcer or bleeding problems; if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5, or have had a reaction to them.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (D84300ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a head cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day after meals, with at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age or an older person; if you have an allergic constitution, high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision), difficulty passing urine, thyroid disease or diabetes; if you are debilitated or have a high fever; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines), other oral medicines for rhinitis, or oral medicines containing an antihistamine (cold medicines, antitussives and expectorants, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If haemorrhagic stroke, nausea, vomiting, persistent or severe thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash, redness, itching, difficulty passing urine, headache, facial flushing or unusual sensitivity to light appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (A16500CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for whitening the teeth.
groups.usage: First check that the mouth is healthy, then brush the teeth thoroughly and keep the mouth clean. Make an impression of the teeth to produce a model, and on the model apply block-out resin 0.5 mm thick over the front of the teeth that are to be whitened, to create space for the material. Cure the model in a light-curing unit for 30 seconds. Using the cured model and an Omnivac, make the plastic tray that will be fitted on the teeth. Trim the tray with scissors to fit the teeth, cutting from 0.5 mm above the gum line, then fill the tray about 1/2 full with the gel. Fit the tray on the teeth, brush off any gel that comes out beyond the gums, and brush the teeth. Wear the tray 1 time each day for about 4 hours, for about 10 days.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have an infection or a wound inside the mouth, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if the user is under 18 years of age.

This medicine must not be eaten; if it is swallowed by mistake, make yourself vomit immediately. Where possible, keep it from touching the gums directly; if it does touch them, rinse with water immediately. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, rinse them with water immediately.

Avoid tobacco, coffee and juice.

Irritation of the gums, the teeth and the digestive tract may occur (in severe cases it may cause inflammation).

summaryTable.What it is for: Whitening of the teeth

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or have had an allergic reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

groups.title: Capsule (461101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to regulate the bowel and improve the symptoms of diarrhoea by normalising the intestinal flora.
groups.usage: Adults: swallow 2 to 8 capsules a day whole with water, without opening them.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. To replace the fluid lost through diarrhoea, drink plenty of fluids that contain salt or sugar.

Eat mainly cooked meat and rice, and avoid raw food, fruit, vegetables, spicy food and frozen food or drinks.

groups.title: Tablet (E21500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and to relieve the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoid symptoms that go with constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times a day, before meals (between meals or before meals). Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day, in the morning and in the evening on an empty stomach (before meals or between meals). Leave at least 4 hours between doses. For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or reduce it a little at a time while watching the form and condition of the stools.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or under, or if you have an acute abdominal condition (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel).

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you have severe abdominal pain or nausea and vomiting, if you have kidney impairment, or if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with antacids. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Prolonged-release tablet (172807ATR)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, low back pain, period pain, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft-tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft-tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day; up to 3200 mg a day may be taken. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight a day, divided into 2 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults take 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day. Do not take more than the recommended dose.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause bleeding in the digestive tract.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or have had them in the past; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have bronchial asthma or have had it in the past; if you have had asthma, hives or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors); if you have pain before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); if you are in the last three months of pregnancy; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had a hypersensitivity reaction; if you have or have had a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver cirrhosis or liver impairment, or kidney impairment; if you have heart failure or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if the user is an older person or a child; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not take more than the recommended dose. Without the advice of a doctor or a pharmacist, do not take this medicine for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or 5 days (children), or for fever for more than 3 days.

Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, low-dose aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin and the like) or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

If signs of shock (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, low white blood cell count, low platelet count, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or raised eosinophils; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, blood in the stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, inflammation of the mouth, abdominal bloating, mouth ulcers, constipation or black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reaction, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or ALP, or liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, hives, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, asthma, bronchial constriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as blind areas in the field of vision, deafness, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, dizziness, drowsiness, light-headedness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness); a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute kidney failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised swelling with shortness of breath and lassitude, Conn's syndrome, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, lassitude, fever, nosebleed or swelling of the limbs appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral suspension (D43400ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to improve acid reflux, heartburn and the indigestion caused by reflux of stomach contents (for example after a meal, during pregnancy, or together with reflux oesophagitis).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 10 to 20 mL at a time, 4 times a day (after meals and before going to bed).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you need to restrict sodium strictly, for example because of congestive heart failure or kidney impairment; if you have high blood calcium, nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-containing kidney stones; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If symptoms are not improved after 7 days of treatment, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

When taking this medicine with tetracycline, digoxin, fluoroquinolones, iron salts, ketoconazole, neuroleptics, thyroxine, penicillamine, beta-blockers (atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), glucocorticoids, chloroquine, estramustine, diphosphonates and the like, leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If an allergic reaction such as itching, bronchial constriction or an anaphylactic reaction appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (B04700CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eczema, dermatitis, prickly heat, dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like, itching, chilblains, insect bites and hives.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) several times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine on infants aged 30 months or under, in or around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on eczema, on wounded skin or on sensitive skin. In particular, do not use a large amount on broken skin surfaces or on areas with blisters.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had an allergic reaction to a medicine, a cosmetic or the like (for example rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching or dermatitis caused by lacquer); if you have an allergic constitution; if you have severe wet or eroded (macerated) skin; if the user is a child; if you have a circulatory disorder or diabetes; or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine externally only; it must not be used internally or inhaled. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, rinse the eyes with water immediately. Shake well before use (external solutions only). If a large amount is absorbed, symptoms of poisoning may occur, so avoid using it over a wide area for a long period. If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching or swelling appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
